criteria.dual_build_agreement: Produce two builds of the modified tree, one via the R-seed toolchain and one via the candidate toolchain, then insist on exact bundle equality (bin/canlc plus catalogue and runtime inputs) and exact output equality across the predecessor corpus joined with the new-feature corpus. The match between the builds is what counts as observation, leaving neither build as the sole source of truth; every mismatch blocks promotion. New abilities beyond what the seed-built binary can run are kept out of the equality check and instead pinned by fixed vectors with bridge assumptions.
criteria.fixed_vectors: Hand-write the expected results for each new binding and behavior (can.std.test@1 operations, http_peer operations, test_launch and dispatch conduct) from the governing contracts alone: catalogue operation definitions, checker admission rules, emitter mappings. A reviewer independent of all builds approves them. Recording any binary's output as expected is forbidden. The seed-built binary and the candidate-built binary each replay the whole vector set byte-for-byte; any deviation in either build stops promotion.
criteria.seed_built_oracle: Use the R-seed toolchain with its reviewed bootstrap steps (go1.27.1, pinned inputs) to compile the modified compiler and runtime. Execute the new-feature corpus with that seed-built bin/canlc and treat its output as the originating observation for every new feature. The candidate-built binary replays those observations byte-for-byte without originating any. Where the seed-built binary cannot execute a new capability, substitute a hand-reviewed fixed vector and document the bootstrap gap in an explicit bridge assumption.

observation_origin.instructions: How should the independent new-feature observations for R-core promotion be originated so the new generation cannot qualify its own new capabilities?
